text: Run the per-pixel net on matrix hardware via cooperative vectors (VK_NV_cooperative_vector / a KHR successor) where the driver offers it
description: Our net is exactly the case cooperative vectors target: every fragment evaluates its own small MLP (132→32→16→8), weights loaded on demand from a buffer. Today it runs as fp16 packed FMAs (experiments c30bda7, 6.3 ms on Vega at 700 MHz). Check: which Vulkan drivers (RADV, Turnip/Adreno 750 on the Frame, NVIDIA desktop) expose cooperative vectors or cooperative matrix in 2026; if any do, add a variant of net.frag behind a feature check, keeping the fp16 path as fallback. Sources: docs.vulkan.org VK_NV_cooperative_vector proposal; NVIDIA neural-shading blog.

status.comment: Checked locally: Mesa 26.2.4 RADV on Renoir (Vega, gfx90c) exposes neither cooperative matrix nor cooperative vector (vulkaninfo); shaderFloat16 = true, so fp16 is the right path here. Still to check: Turnip on the Frame's Adreno 750 (run vulkaninfo on the device).
